literal: A country they say is that which has wealth without seeking; not a country is that which gives wealth when sought.
translation: They say a true country is one that yields wealth without requiring laborious search; a land that yields wealth only when sought is no country at all.
modern: முயற்சி செய்து தேடாமலேயே வளம் தரும் நாடே சிறந்த நாடு என்று கூறுவர்; தேடி முயற்சி செய்தால் மட்டுமே வளம் தரும் நாடு ஒரு நாடாகாது.
explanation: This couplet defines the ideal country based on its natural abundance. A truly great nation is one where resources and wealth are naturally plentiful, requiring no painful struggle or desperate seeking by its citizens. Conversely, a land where people must toil excessively and search hard just to obtain basic wealth does not deserve to be called a true country. The word 'நாடா' (without seeking) highlights effortless prosperity, while 'நாட' (upon seeking) emphasizes the burden of forced labor to extract wealth.
